summary.text: Andrew Govanstone is standing for Labor in South-West Coast at the 2026 Victorian election, a seat held by the Liberals' Roma Britnell. He is from Portland, and the ABC's candidate notes say his work has included community engagement for the state's Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action. His Labor page lists a campaign email and social accounts but carries no biography.

occupation.text: Community engagement officer, Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action
occupation.note: The ABC says he has worked in this role; it does not say whether he still does.

sources.title: South-West Coast: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Andrew Govanstone, Labor candidate for South-West Coast, Victorian Labor

summary.text: Hera Sheppard is standing for the Victorian Socialists in South-West Coast at the 2026 Victorian election. She has lived in Warrnambool all her life and is still a school student, and she calls herself one of the youngest candidates a party has endorsed for parliament. A member of the Retail and Fast Food Workers' Union, she says she helped organise her fast-food workplace for the first time.

prior_roles.organisation: Retail and Fast Food Workers' Union

priorities.text: Upgrading the Warrnambool rail line to 160 km/h for faster, safer trips
Ending the sale of public housing and filling empty homes while the waiting list grows
Backing teachers in their industrial campaign
I aim to represent the next generation of young workers

sources.title: South-West Coast: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Richard Hughes is One Nation's candidate for South-West Coast at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's candidate notes say he has been with Victoria Police for over 28 years and is now a detective in Warrnambool's Crime Investigation Unit, with cases in the region including drug trafficking and arson. One Nation's page for him could not be read for this profile because the site refuses automated requests.

sources.title: South-West Coast: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Roma Britnell is the Liberal MP for South-West Coast, first elected at the October 2015 by-election that followed Denis Napthine's retirement. She was a nurse for about 30 years, managed an Aboriginal community health service at Framlingham and ran a dairy farm. She has held shadow portfolios including ports and freight and child protection, and has been Shadow Cabinet Secretary since February 2026. She is recontesting South-West Coast in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Shadow Assistant Minister for Roads and Road Safety
Shadow Minister for Ports and Freight
Shadow Minister for Boating and Fishing

priorities.text: A fair share of government funding for the region
Investment in regional infrastructure and services to support growth
Decentralisation, with growth in regional centres easing pressure on Melbourne

summary.text: Silver Rose Watts is the Greens candidate for South-West Coast at the 2026 Victorian election. She lives in Warrnambool, where she has studied and worked, and she describes herself as a youth worker, facilitator and student. Her campaign centres on living costs, housing, health care and the local environment.

priorities.text: advocate for people over profits in every policy decision

sources.title: South-West Coast: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Tamhas Buchan is the Family First candidate for South-West Coast at the 2026 Victorian election. He owns a small business that helps other businesses attract customers online, and the ABC notes he earlier worked in executive search for the finance industry in Hong Kong and Sydney. His party page says he grew up in country Victoria and is married with three children.

occupation.text: Marketing consultant and small business owner

prior_roles.role: Search consultant, finance sector (Hong Kong and Sydney)

priorities.text: Easing living costs for families, including taxes and power and fuel bills
Support for young couples wanting to have children
Opposing abortion and euthanasia, and protecting free speech and religious freedom
Lower and slower immigration, limited to skilled migrants and genuine refugees
Parental rights, personal privacy and more open government
